newsitem.title: CHINA: China landslide kills three, leaves 147 missing.
newsitem.headline: China landslide kills three, leaves 147 missing.

text.p: A huge landslide triggered by torrential rains in China's mountainous southwestern Sichuan province has killed at least three people and left 147 missing, a provincial official said on Tuesday.

The landslide crashed down on four villages in Meigu county in the early hours of June 5, burying residents of the district in the southern part of the province as they slept, the official said by telephone from the provincial capital, Chengdu.

Rescue workers had recovered three bodies and were searching for another 147 people still missing after the huge slide, which measured 2,000 metres (6,500 ft) long and 700 metres (2,300 ft) wide, roared over the villages, he said.
A night of torrential rain and hailstorms in the mountainous area triggered the landslide, officials and media reports said.
The disaster affected 1,527 people in the area and left two seriously injured, the Sichuan official said.
The death toll could rise to as high as 110 after bodies of the missing were recovered, the Yangcheng Evening News said in an edition available in Beijing on Tuesday.
The landslide damaged 307 houses and left 294 people homeless, an official of Sichuan Daily newspaper said.
The disaster also destroyed farmland and disrupted traffic, communications and power supply in the area, he said.
